thesis.main_shareholders: The Ökoworld Foundation (a charitable foundation) now holds the majority of voting ordinary shares (3.95 million ordinary shares, unlisted), after founders Klaus Odenthal and Angelika Grote and early shareholders transferred their shares to the foundation; non-voting preference shares (3.05 million) trade publicly ([Private Banking Magazin](https://www.private-banking-magazin.de/oekoworld-foundation-wird-mehrheitliche-stammaktionaerin-der-oekoworld/))
thesis.insider_ownership: Founders' shares were consolidated into the charitable Ökoworld Foundation, meaning future dividends on ordinary shares flow to charitable projects rather than to individual founders directly; founder Klaus Odenthal remains active on the supervisory board ([Private Banking Magazin](https://www.private-banking-magazin.de/oekoworld-foundation-wird-mehrheitliche-stammaktionaerin-der-oekoworld/))
thesis.red_flags: None identified from sources reviewed; the foundation-based control structure is unusual but was a deliberate, disclosed restructuring rather than a governance concern.

thesis.business_description: Spyrosoft S.A. is a Poland-based (Wrocław, founded 2016) software engineering company providing custom software development, cloud, embedded engineering, AI/ML, product design and technology-consulting services to clients in automotive, healthcare/life sciences, financial services, geospatial and other industries.
thesis.competitive_position: Spyrosoft is a fast-growing mid-sized Polish IT services/software-engineering company competing in the broader European nearshore-outsourcing and engineering-services market, differentiated by sector specialization (notably automotive and embedded systems) rather than being a generic staffing provider. [EMIS company profile](https://www.emis.com/php/company-profile/PL/Spyrosoft_SA_en_4370759.html)
thesis.main_shareholders: The company is majority-controlled by its founders: Konrad Weiske (~30.71%), Dorota Łekawa (~25.08%) and Wioletta Bodnarus (~24.98%), with remaining shares (~19.24%) held by others/free float. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/SPYROSOFT-SP-LKA-AKCYJNA-123687631/company/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Founders Konrad Weiske, Dorota Łekawa and Wioletta Bodnarus collectively hold approximately 80.8% of shares, representing very high founder/insider ownership. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/SPYROSOFT-SP-LKA-AKCYJNA-123687631/company/)
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Gesco SE is a German investment holding company, founded in 1989, that acquires and develops economically sound industrial small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) for the long term, organized in Process technology, Resource technology, and Healthcare/Infrastructure technology segments.
thesis.competitive_position: A long-standing, publicly listed (since 1998) German SME holding company that provides capital-markets access to owner-managed industrial businesses; ownership is broadly dispersed with no single controlling shareholder. [Gesco Annual Report 2025](https://gesco.de/fileadmin/static/pdfs/en/investor_relations/financial_reports/2025/2025-gesco-annual_report.pdf)
thesis.main_shareholders: Investor Norman Rentrop holds approximately 14.5% and entrepreneur Stefan Heimöller holds approximately 14.2%; Baden-Württembergische Versorgungsanstalt für Ärzte, Zahnärzte und Tierärzte has reported crossing the 3% disclosure threshold; free float is approximately 66.8% across roughly 8,300 registered shareholders. [Gesco Shareholders](https://gesco.de/en/investor-relations/shares)
thesis.insider_ownership: No founder-family or management insider control was identified; the two largest holders (Rentrop and Heimöller) are described as outside investor/entrepreneur shareholders rather than company management, and the remainder is widely held. Not disclosed as a management-held stake in sources reviewed.
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in available search results.

thesis.business_description: PCC Exol S.A. is a Polish manufacturer of surfactants used in household chemicals, personal care, textiles, paper and metallurgical industries, headquartered in Brzeg Dolny, Poland.
thesis.competitive_position: A mid-sized Central European surfactants producer and one of only two PCC Group companies listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (alongside PCC Rokita), operating as part of the larger German PCC SE chemicals conglomerate. [PCC Group Structure](https://pcc.eu/en/company/group-structure/)
thesis.main_shareholders: Parent company PCC SE (a German holding company) holds approximately 87.09% of PCC Exol S.A.; the remainder is free float from its 2012 partial IPO. PCC SE's sole shareholder is reported to be Waldemar Preussner, chairman of PCC SE's supervisory board. [Wikipedia/PCC SE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PCC_SE)
thesis.insider_ownership: Ultimate insider control rests with Waldemar Preussner as sole shareholder of parent PCC SE, which in turn owns ~87% of PCC Exol; no separate PCC Exol management ownership stake was identified in sources reviewed. [Wikipedia/PCC SE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PCC_SE)
thesis.red_flags: High related-party concentration risk: ~87% parent ownership by PCC SE means minority (free-float) shareholders have limited influence over strategy and related-party transactions within the PCC Group; no specific litigation or fraud finding was identified in sources reviewed.

thesis.business_description: PayPoint plc is a UK-based payments and commerce company operating across Shopping, E-Commerce, Payments and Banking, and Love2shop divisions, providing a range of payment acceptance, card processing, Open Banking, direct debit and cash-handling services to retailers, billers and consumers.
thesis.competitive_position: An established UK payments/commerce platform (MultiPay) with net revenue growth of 17.9% year-on-year in its most recent reported period, competing against payment specialists such as EVO Payments, Paymentus and larger players like Stripe; the company has historically held a strong position in UK prepayment/bill-payment services though this has drawn regulatory scrutiny (see red flags). [MarketScreener](https://uk.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/PAYPOINT-PLC-4004860/company/)
thesis.main_shareholders: Invermob Coruña SL holds approximately 32.15%; Inversis Gestión SGIIC holds approximately 8.2%; Santander Asset Management holds approximately 6.78%; Brown Capital Management holds approximately 5.42%; institutional investors comprise approximately 71.98% of the shareholder base overall. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/PAYPOINT-PLC-120960517/company-shareholders/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Not disclosed as a significant founder/management stake in sources reviewed; the register is dominated by institutional/financial investors (notably Spain-linked Invermob Coruña SL) rather than company insiders.
thesis.red_flags: A UK Competition Appeal Tribunal found PayPoint had abused its dominant position in the pre-pay energy market (historical infringement on contracts that ceased in 2018), in a case brought by competitor Global 365/energy supplier Utilita; PayPoint largely defeated the GBP 172.2 million claim (awarded damages of only ~GBP 169,334 plus interest, over 99.8% reduction) but was ordered to pay roughly GBP 1.5 million toward the claimant's legal costs; separately, Ofgem's earlier investigation into PayPoint's prepayment-market conduct led the company to make voluntary commitments and a GBP 12.5 million donation to Ofgem's redress fund; the company was also separately sued by a fuel-poverty charity. [Global Competition Review](https://globalcompetitionreview.com/article/paypoint-damages-claim-cut-more-99)

thesis.business_description: Belgian company (incorporated 1996, headquartered in Zaventem) supplying electronic payment terminals, transaction processing software and related services (installation, support, tokenization via S-token, e-payment platform SET2U) mainly to small and mid-sized merchants.
thesis.competitive_position: A small, Belgium-focused payments provider (~52 employees, ~$23.5M trailing revenue) with 86% of sales domestic; niche player relative to larger pan-European payment processors, with revenue split across card transaction management (45.3%), terminals (41.1%) and software (13.6%).
thesis.main_shareholders: Major disclosed holders (via >5% transparency declarations) include Big Friend NV, Powergraph BV, Drupafina and Think Media NV; private companies hold ~64% of shares in aggregate, general public ~29% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/be/diversified-financials/ebr-keyw/keyware-technologies-shares/ownership))
thesis.insider_ownership: Insiders collectively hold a modest stake (~€1.0m of the ~€21m company) largely through private-company holding vehicles rather than direct individual ownership ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/be/diversified-financials/ebr-keyw/keyware-technologies-shares/ownership))
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; small market cap (~€21m) and concentrated private-company ownership warrant governance attention.

thesis.business_description: Intred S.p.A. is an Italian telecommunications provider based in Brescia that builds and operates proprietary fiber-optic broadband infrastructure (15,000+ km of network) for residential and business customers, primarily in Lombardy.
thesis.competitive_position: Intred has built a strong regional position with full ownership of its fiber network across Brescia, Milan and Bergamo provinces (45,000+ customers, over €160m in technology investment), giving it service-quality and response-time advantages versus resellers; however, its footprint is geographically concentrated in Lombardy (despite an OpenFiber partnership), limiting national scale versus larger Italian telecom operators, and it has been pursuing an uplisting to Euronext Milan to support further growth.
thesis.main_shareholders: DM Holding S.r.l. (controlled 67% by Daniele Peli and 33% by Marisa Prati) ~60.3-60.4%, Value First SICAF / First Sicaf S.p.A. ~9.4%, free float ~30.2-30.3% ([Borsa Italiana](https://www.borsaitaliana.it/borsa/azioni/profilo-societa-dettaglio.html?isin=IT0005337818&lang=en))
thesis.insider_ownership: ~60.3% held by founder/Chairman-CEO Daniele Peli and his wife Marisa Prati via DM Holding S.r.l.
thesis.red_flags: Geographic concentration risk: operations remain limited to Lombardy, which supports service quality locally but constrains addressable market versus national fiber operators; no accounting, litigation or regulatory red flags were identified from official sources in this search.

thesis.business_description: CANCOM SE is a German IT infrastructure and services provider, founded in 1992 and headquartered in Munich, operating Cloud Solutions and IT Solutions segments (IT strategy, system integration, managed services) primarily in Germany and Austria.
thesis.competitive_position: A leading German/Austrian IT systems integrator and managed-services provider that has grown via acquisition (e.g., K-Businesscom AG, Austria's leading ICT provider with ~1,650 employees, expanding reach into Switzerland, Romania and the Czech Republic); competes with larger global IT service providers and regional integrators. [CANCOM company facts](https://www.cancom.de/en/company/cancom-se/about-cancom/)
thesis.main_shareholders: Free float is approximately 57.51%; Primepulse SE (the investment holding co-founded by CANCOM founder Klaus Weinmann) holds approximately 15.00%; other notable holders include K & K Stiftung (~6.49%), SEO Management AG (~5.04%), Allianz Global Investors (~4.98%), Union Investment (~4.87%), Goldman Sachs (~4.77%), BlackRock (~3.17%) and Johannes Mohn (~3.15%). [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/CANCOM-SE-435885/company-shareholders/)
thesis.insider_ownership: CANCOM co-founder Klaus Weinmann exercises significant influence through Primepulse SE's ~15% stake and, as of October 2023, his court-ordered appointment to and chairmanship of CANCOM's Supervisory Board, raising potential related-party/conflict-of-interest considerations given his continued operational role at Primepulse. [Stock3/Primepulse](https://primepulse.com/unternehmen/)
thesis.red_flags: CANCOM issued a profit warning shortly after having raised its own forecast, described in press commentary as an 'embarrassing' guidance reversal; additionally, founder Klaus Weinmann holds overlapping roles as CANCOM Supervisory Board Chairman and CEO of Primepulse SE (a ~15% CANCOM shareholder), which raises potential conflict-of-interest questions around capital allocation and related-party dealings. [Stock3](https://stock3.com/news/cancom-gruender-greift-erneut-bei-der-aktie-zu-12970591)

thesis.business_description: Hawesko Holding SE is a German wine, champagne and spirits trading group, operating through retail (Jacques' Wein-Depot, Wein & Co.), B2B wholesale (Wein Wolf, Grand Cru Select) and e-commerce (Hawesko, WirWinzer) segments.
thesis.competitive_position: Hawesko describes itself as one of Europe's leading wine merchants, with a multi-channel model spanning specialist retail stores, B2B wholesale distribution and e-commerce, plus subsidiaries abroad (e.g. an 80%-owned Czech operation, Global Wines & Spirits). The multi-brand, multi-channel structure gives it scale advantages in sourcing and logistics versus independent wine shops, though it faces competition from supermarket wine ranges and pure online retailers. [Hawesko Holding corporate info](https://eqs-news.com/company/hawesko-holding-se/info/5b75b6ff-ea7c-11e8-902f-2c44fd856d8c)
thesis.main_shareholders: Detlev Meyer controls the company through his wholly-owned holding vehicle Tocos Beteiligung GmbH, reported at roughly 72.7% of shares as of 31 December 2024 ([MarketScreener insider profile](https://ae.marketscreener.com/insider/DETLEV-MEYER-A0DAG8/)); free float is the remainder (~21-28% depending on the date of the snapshot) ([TradingView financials overview](https://se.tradingview.com/symbols/XETR-HAW/financials-overview)).
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is effectively Detlev Meyer's controlling stake via Tocos (~72-73%); he built this from an initial ~29.5% stake via a 2014-2015 takeover offer that ultimately crossed 75-79% of voting shares before settling near its current level ([Meininger/Börsen-Zeitung takeover coverage](https://www.meininger.de/wein/handel/hawesko-endgueltig-gekapert)).
thesis.red_flags: Historical (2014-2015) public governance dispute: then-CEO and major shareholder Alexander Margaritoff publicly accused incoming majority owner Detlev Meyer of disguising his real motive (control) behind a dividend-policy disagreement, and Margaritoff subsequently resigned and sold his stake; this is a decade-old conflict with no evidence of ongoing dispute found. [Börsen-Zeitung interview with Margaritoff](https://www.boersen-zeitung.de/unternehmen-branchen/herrn-meyers-verhalten-ist-nicht-freundlich)

thesis.business_description: ChemoMetec A/S is a Danish developer, manufacturer and seller of analytical instruments (the NucleoCounter range) for quantitative cell counting and analysis, serving cell and gene therapy, cancer/stem cell research, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and animal semen/milk quality-control applications.
thesis.competitive_position: ChemoMetec holds a specialized niche in automated cell-counting instrumentation (Instruments, Consumables, and research-partnership segments), serving life-science, biopharma and agricultural end markets; scale is small relative to broad-based lab-instrument conglomerates, but its NucleoCounter platform has established recurring consumables revenue.
thesis.main_shareholders: BlackRock, Inc. (~14.2%), SEB Investment Management AB (~5.83%), The Vanguard Group, Inc. (~3.96%), Hans Glensbjerg (~3.67%) ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/kind-shareholders-own-chemometec-cph-040240651.html))
thesis.insider_ownership: Individual insiders hold approximately 3.75% of the company, per Simply Wall St ownership data; institutions hold ~33% and the general public ~63.2%
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in this search.

thesis.business_description: Cinkarna Celje, d. d. is a Slovenian chemical processing company, operating for over 150 years, that produces and markets titanium dioxide pigment along with construction chemicals (sealants, facade plasters, mortars, waterproofing agents) and copper/sulfur fungicides.
thesis.competitive_position: A long-established, vertically diversified Slovenian chemicals producer that transitioned from metallurgy (pre-1968) to titanium dioxide pigment production (from 1973) and diversified further into construction chemicals and agrochemicals; among the most resilient companies in the Slovenian economy given its long operating history. [Cinkarna company profile](https://www.cinkarna.si/en/about-the-company)
thesis.main_shareholders: SDH d.d. (Slovenia's state-owned Slovenian Sovereign Holding) holds approximately 24.44%; Modra zavarovalnica d.d. (a Slovenian pension/insurance fund) holds approximately 20.17%; UniCredit Bank Austria AG (as nominee/FID) holds approximately 4.33%; TR5 d.o.o. holds approximately 4.2%. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/CINKARNA-CELJE-D-D-11360089/company/)
thesis.insider_ownership: No specific founder/management insider ownership was identified; the largest shareholders are the Slovenian state holding company (SDH) and an insurance/pension fund (Modra zavarovalnica) rather than company insiders. Not disclosed as a management stake in sources reviewed.
thesis.red_flags: As a long-running titanium dioxide and chemicals producer, the company operates in an industry with inherent environmental/regulatory exposure (it references holding an integrated IPPC environmental permit), but no specific pollution lawsuit, litigation or governance dispute was identified in available search results. None identified from official sources reviewed.

thesis.business_description: Renta Corporación Real Estate, S.A. is a Barcelona-based Spanish real estate company, founded in 1991, that acquires, refurbishes/rehabilitates and sells residential, office, retail, logistics and hotel properties in Barcelona, Madrid and internationally (Germany, UK).
thesis.competitive_position: Renta Corporación operates a value-add 'buy-refurbish-sell' real estate trading model rather than long-term holding, with a market cap of roughly $29.7m and trailing revenue of about $51.2m (2025); it recently brought in BC Partners as a 30% partner in its self-storage business, indicating a strategy of partnering with larger capital providers to scale niche real estate segments ([El Economista](https://www.eleconomista.es/vivienda-inmobiliario/noticias/13073774/11/24/bc-partners-toma-el-30-del-negocio-de-trasteros-de-renta-corporacion.html)).
thesis.main_shareholders: Luis Hernández de Cabanyes, founder and executive president/CEO (39.26%), Dinomen S.L. (10.82%), Blas Herrero Fernández (7.94%), Aurodoc 75 S.L. (6.28%) ([Yahoo Finanzas](https://es.finance.yahoo.com/quote/REN.MC/holders/))
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder and CEO Luis Hernández de Cabanyes holds 39.26% of the company, making it founder-controlled ([Yahoo Finanzas](https://es.finance.yahoo.com/quote/REN.MC/holders/))
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in this search; the company's opportunistic buy-refurbish-sell real estate trading model carries inherent cyclicality/market-timing risk versus buy-and-hold REITs, though no specific governance issue was found.

thesis.business_description: Jæren Sparebank is a Norwegian regional savings bank headquartered in Bryne, formed from the 2015 merger of Time Sparebank and Klepp Sparebank, serving personal, agricultural, and SME customers through branches in the Jæren region. [Jæren Sparebank - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A6ren_Sparebank)
thesis.competitive_position: Jæren Sparebank is a small local savings bank with a regional branch network in the Jæren area of Norway, structured as a Norwegian savings bank with equity certificates (a hybrid ownership form) rather than ordinary shares; by law equity-certificate holders can hold at most 40% of votes, which protects against takeover but also caps outside investor control. [About equity certificates](https://www.sparebank1.no/en/ostlandet/about-us/investor/equity-certificate/about-equity-certificates.html)
thesis.main_shareholders: Major holders of Jæren Sparebank's equity certificates include Sparebankstiftinga Time og Hå (~50.92%), Sparebankstiftelsen Klepp (~12.27%), Eika Kapitalforvaltning AS (~8.45%), Oddvar Salte (~3.04%), and KLP Kapitalforvaltning AS (~2.23%). [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/JAEREN-SPAREBANK-1413187/company/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Ownership is dominated by two local savings-bank foundations (Sparebankstiftinga Time og Hå and Sparebankstiftelsen Klepp, together holding over 63%) rather than by bank management or individual insiders; one named individual holder, Oddvar Salte, holds approximately 3.04%. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/JAEREN-SPAREBANK-1413187/company/)
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources searched.

thesis.business_description: Nilörngruppen AB is a Sweden-based company that designs and manufactures garment labels and branding/identity solutions for fashion and apparel brands, with offices and manufacturing in Sweden, Denmark, Germany, the UK, Portugal, Turkey, Hong Kong, and India. [Nilörn investors page](https://www.nilorn.com/investors/)
thesis.competitive_position: Nilörngruppen is a specialized global garment-label and brand-identity supplier serving fashion houses internationally, backed by private-equity-style parent AB Traction; it recently became the subject of a public takeover offer from Trimco Group, a larger global label/trim competitor, suggesting strategic consolidation interest in the sector. [Nilörngruppen board statement on Trimco Group takeover offer](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/04/3286410/0/en/Nil%C3%B6rngruppen-publishes-Board-statement-in-connection-with-public-takeover-offer-from-Trimco-Group.html)
thesis.main_shareholders: AB Traction is the controlling shareholder, holding approximately 26.31% of share capital and about 58.08% of voting rights (as of Sept 30, 2025) via dual-class shares; AB Traction is itself a family-run investment vehicle, over 80% owned by the Stillström family. [Nilörn largest shareholder page](https://www.nilorn.com/investors/the-share/largest-shareholder/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider/controlling ownership is concentrated via AB Traction, led by CEO Petter Stillström, who also chairs Nilörngruppen's board; Traction holds 100% of Nilörn's A-shares, giving the Stillström family effective control despite a minority economic stake. Reflecting this conflict, Petter Stillström recused himself from the board's evaluation of the 2026 Trimco Group takeover offer. [GlobeNewswire: Nilörngruppen board statement](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/04/3286410/0/en/Nil%C3%B6rngruppen-publishes-Board-statement-in-connection-with-public-takeover-offer-from-Trimco-Group.html)
thesis.red_flags: A structural governance point: the Chairman (Petter Stillström) is simultaneously CEO of the controlling shareholder (AB Traction), creating an inherent related-party dynamic that required him to recuse himself from a 2026 takeover-offer evaluation; this is disclosed and managed via recusal rather than being a hidden conflict. No other lawsuit or scandal was identified. [Nilörngruppen board statement on Trimco Group offer](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/04/3286410/0/en/Nil%C3%B6rngruppen-publishes-Board-statement-in-connection-with-public-takeover-offer-from-Trimco-Group.html)

thesis.business_description: Miquel y Costas & Miquel, S.A. is a Spain-based company, with roots dating to 1725, that produces fine and lightweight specialty papers, primarily for the tobacco (cigarette paper) industry, and is one of only four cigarette-paper manufacturers in the world. [Miquel y Costas Miquel S.A. - Encyclopedia.com](https://www.encyclopedia.com/books/politics-and-business-magazines/miquel-y-costas-miquel-sa)
thesis.competitive_position: Miquel y Costas holds a globally scarce competitive position as one of only four manufacturers of cigarette paper worldwide, a niche with high barriers to entry given specialized know-how and long-standing customer relationships built over nearly 300 years of operating history. [Miquel y Costas corporate information](https://miquelycostas.com/en/corporate-information/)
thesis.main_shareholders: Major shareholders include Jorge Mercader Miró (~18.17%), Indumenta Pueri SL (~14.65%), Bernadette Miquel Vacarisas (~12.36%), and Miquel María Del Carmen Escasany (~9.0%); descendants of the founding Miquel y Costas family remain prominent shareholders alongside Chairman Jorge Mercader Miró. thesis.business_description: PCC Rokita SA is a Poland-based chemicals producer headquartered in Brzeg Dolny, operating primarily in polyols/polyurethane precursor chemicals and other specialty chemical products, and is described as one of the largest chemical companies in Poland and the largest in Lower Silesia. thesis.competitive_position: PCC Rokita is a leading Polish chemicals producer, particularly in polyether polyols for polyurethane production, benefiting from being part of the larger PCC SE group's integrated chemicals/raw-materials/energy/logistics platform. thesis.main_shareholders: PCC SE (headquartered in Duisburg, Germany) is the controlling shareholder, holding approximately 84.26% of PCC Rokita SA, with the remainder free-floated on the Warsaw Stock Exchange since a 2014 IPO of a minority stake. thesis.business_description: Altri, SGPS, S.A. is a Portuguese industrial group that manages eucalyptus forests and produces and sells wood/eucalyptus pulp (including kraft and bleached hardwood/eucalyptus pulp) through mills including Celbi, Celtejo, and Caima, with combined capacity of around 1.2 million tonnes/year, plus co-generation of renewable energy. [Altri - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altri)
thesis.competitive_position: Altri is a major European eucalyptus pulp producer with scale advantages from owning its own forest/timber supply and multiple mills; it was spun out of the Cofina group's industrial assets and continues to expand (e.g., acquiring a controlling stake in green-fibre producer AeoniQ), though it faces resistance to expansion projects on environmental grounds. [Altri AeoniQ acquisition](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/altri-sgps-acquires-controlling-stake-113404898.html)
thesis.main_shareholders: Reported major shareholders include Ana R. de C. Menéres de Mendonça (~17.54%), Caderno Azul-SGPS SA (~16.67%), Paulo Jorge dos Santos Fernandes (~13.63%), and Pedro Miguel Matos Borges de Oliveira (~12.35%); these holders are linked to the company's founding/controlling group originating from the Cofina spin-out. [MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ALTRI-SGPS-S-A-5808/company/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Ownership is concentrated among a small group of individual/family-linked holders tied to the company's founding structure (Menéres de Mendonça, Caderno Azul SGPS, Santos Fernandes, Matos Borges de Oliveira), collectively holding roughly 60% combined per the figures found, rather than being widely dispersed among unrelated institutions. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ALTRI-SGPS-S-A-5808/company/)
thesis.red_flags: Altri's planned new pulp mill in Galicia, Spain has drawn significant opposition from local communities and a coalition of 52 NGOs over environmental impact in an ecologically sensitive Natura 2000 area, and the project has sought roughly €250 million in EU NextGenerationEU funding, which has raised additional public scrutiny; separately, the company previously announced it terminated pulp deliveries to Russia following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine (a disclosed compliance action, not a red flag itself). [Altri's pulp mill in Galicia: a battle for the region's future](https://meta.eeb.org/2025/04/03/altris-pulp-mill-in-galicia-a-battle-for-the-future-of-the-region/)

thesis.business_description: Asseco South Eastern Europe S.A. is a Poland-based holding company providing IT consulting and software services across the Balkans, Turkey and Romania, operating as part of the broader Asseco Group federation of companies.
thesis.competitive_position: A regional IT services arm of the Asseco Group (a federation of listed and unlisted companies led by parent Asseco Poland, which does not seek 100% ownership of group members), giving it scale and cross-selling advantages across South-East Europe. [Outsiders' Corner](https://www.outsiderscorner.com/p/asseco-poland)
thesis.main_shareholders: Parent company Asseco Poland S.A. holds approximately 50.89%; PTE Allianz Polska SA holds approximately 16.85%. [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/equities/asseco-south-eastern-europe-ownership)
thesis.insider_ownership: Control is exercised through parent Asseco Poland's ~50.89% stake rather than direct founder/management ownership of ASEE itself; no separate significant management stake was identified. Not disclosed as a distinct insider stake in sources reviewed.
thesis.red_flags: A Serbian governance/conflict-of-interest controversy was reported: Igor Brnabić, brother of former Serbian PM Ana Brnabić, served as a director of Asseco while Asseco's South-Eastern Europe unit held IT contracts with the Serbian government's IT office (headed by the PM), raising public conflict-of-interest questions that went unanswered by relevant institutions. [Serbian Monitor](https://www.serbianmonitor.com/en/the-asseco-affair-and-conflict-of-interest/)

thesis.business_description: Billington Holdings Plc is a UK structural steel and construction safety-solutions group, comprising Billington Structures, Peter Marshall Steel Stairs and Specialist Protective Coatings (structural steelwork) and Easi-Edge and Hoard-It (safety solutions).

thesis.main_shareholders: Top institutional holders include Miton Asset Management / Premier Miton UK Multi Cap Income (275,980 shares each, same holder), Providence Investment Partners (50,000 shares) and Diverse Income Trust (12,500 shares); precise percentage stakes were not confirmed from sources reviewed. thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in available search results.

thesis.business_description: Akwel SA (formerly MGI Coutier) is a French automotive equipment maker that designs, manufactures, and markets fluid-management and mechanisms components for vehicle manufacturers worldwide. [Akwel company profile](https://akwel-automotive.com/en/group/history/)
thesis.competitive_position: Akwel is a long-established, family-controlled Tier 1/2 automotive supplier operating internationally; it is a mid-sized niche component maker rather than a dominant global player, competing in a fragmented auto-parts supply market. thesis.business_description: Dekpol S.A. is a Polish construction and development group based in Pinczyn, providing general-contracting services for industrial, sports and environmental-protection facilities plus road, sanitary and hydro-technical works, manufacturing buckets/attachments for construction machinery, and developing residential and commercial real estate mainly in northern Poland.
thesis.competitive_position: Dekpol combines general contracting with its own residential/commercial development arm and a machinery-attachments manufacturing business, giving it diversified revenue streams versus pure-play developers or contractors in the Tri-City/northern Poland market ([Dekpol](https://dekpol.pl)).
thesis.main_shareholders: OMT Family Foundation, controlled by founder Mariusz Tuchlin (77.33% of votes via 6,466,845 shares), Familiar S.A. SICAV-SIF (8.13%) ([BiznesRadar](https://www.biznesradar.pl/akcjonariat/DEKPOL))
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder Mariusz Tuchlin controls approximately 77.33% of voting rights through the OMT Family Foundation, making Dekpol a tightly founder-controlled company ([BiznesRadar](https://www.biznesradar.pl/akcjonariat/DEKPOL))

thesis.competitive_position: Aktia is a mid-sized Finnish bank with a diversified financial-services model (banking plus asset management and insurance), rooted in historical savings-bank/Åbo Akademi-linked ownership; no independent market-share data was found to size its competitive position versus larger Nordic banks. thesis.insider_ownership: Ownership is concentrated among legacy founding-era families (Etola, von Rettig, Hammarén families) rather than current executive management; these combined family stakes total roughly a third of the company. thesis.business_description: Croatian universal commercial bank (founded October 1991, originally by Croatian Post) offering retail, corporate and public-sector banking products, distinguished by a distribution network combining its own branches (68 as of March 2024) with financial-service counters located in Croatian Post offices nationwide.
thesis.competitive_position: The largest financial institution in Croatian domestic ownership, with total assets of €7.046bn and net income of €80.6M (2023); its unique Croatian Post branch-network partnership gives it Croatia's largest basic-banking-services distribution footprint versus foreign-owned competitor banks.
thesis.main_shareholders: Republic of Croatia (42.43% direct, ~74.57% combined with state-owned entities), Croatian Post (11.93%), State Agency for Deposit Insurance and Bank Resolution (8.98%), Croatian Pension Insurance Institute (8.76%); state directly/indirectly owns ~77% ([HPB Annual Report 2024](https://www.hpb.hr/UserDocsImages/Financijska-izvjesca/Annual%20Report%20-%2031.12.2024.pdf))
thesis.red_flags: Majority state ownership (~77% direct/indirect via the Republic of Croatia and state entities) creates governance considerations typical of state-controlled banks, including potential political influence over strategy; no specific litigation or compliance issue identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: ABC arbitrage SA is a France-based company that designs and operates arbitrage trading strategies and asset management services across European and American financial markets, exploiting price discrepancies between related financial instruments. [ABC arbitrage - Who we are](https://www.abc-arbitrage.com/who-we-are/)
thesis.competitive_position: ABC arbitrage is described by equity research as a specialist arbitrage trader and asset manager, a niche quantitative strategy business founded in 1995 by Dominique Ceolin (current CEO) and co-founder Xavier Chauderlot; it operates its own capital plus a regulated asset management arm (ABC arbitrage Asset Management), differentiating it from traditional long-only asset managers. [Edison Group: ABC arbitrage - A specialist arbitrage trader and asset manager](https://www.edisongroup.com/research/a-specialist-arbitrage-trader-and-asset-manager/32531/)
thesis.main_shareholders: Major shareholders include Financière WDD (~11.95%), Aubépar Industries (~11.93%, linked to co-founder Xavier Chauderlot), David Hoey (~5.85%), Eximium (~5.06%), and CEO/co-founder Dominique Ceolin (~4.44%); other management holds a further ~6.23%, with free float around 54.26%. [MarketScreener shareholders](https://in.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ABC-ARBITRAGE-5094/company-shareholders/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Founders and management retain meaningful ownership: CEO Dominique Ceolin holds roughly 4.44% personally, co-founder Xavier Chauderlot is linked to Aubépar Industries (~11.93%), and other management collectively hold about 6.23%, putting combined founder/management-linked ownership above 20%. [MarketScreener](https://in.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ABC-ARBITRAGE-5094/company-shareholders/)
thesis.red_flags: No specific lawsuit or regulatory sanction was identified; the company combines CEO/Chairman roles, which it has disclosed and defended via governance counterweights per its own filings, a governance structure worth noting though not flagged as a violation by regulators in the sources found. Could not verify further beyond routine AMF disclosure filings.

thesis.business_description: ORBIS AG (Saarbrücken, Germany) is an IT consulting and software company specializing in SAP-based business solutions and implementation services for mid-sized and large enterprises.
thesis.competitive_position: ORBIS is a niche SAP implementation/consulting specialist rather than a scale software vendor; it has grown via partnerships (e.g., a 2021 strategic cooperation with Hörmann) rather than organic market dominance, positioning it as a smaller regional player in the crowded SAP consulting ecosystem. [ORBIS-Hörmann strategic cooperation announcement](https://orbis.de/en/investor-relations/ad-hoc-announcements/detail/strategic-collaboration-orbis-hoermann.html)
thesis.main_shareholders: Hörmann Digital Beteiligungs GmbH became the controlling shareholder via a 2021 strategic cooperation and share purchases from GMV AG (the former largest shareholder) and other holders; a 2021 voting-rights notice shows Hörmann's direct stake around 34.7% with total voting rights (including instruments/options) near 50% ([ORBIS 2021 board report / GSC Research](https://gsc-research.de/media/2021-04-26_ORBIS.pdf)). Swoctem GmbH (linked to Friedhelm Loh) separately held about 15% of voting rights as of a 2014 disclosure ([ORBIS board report 2022](https://www.orbis.de/fileadmin/dateien/de/downloads/ir/HV/2022/Erlaeuternder_Bericht_des_Vorstands_der_ORBIS_SE_zu_den_Angaben_nach______289a_Abs__1_315a_Abs__1_HGB.pdf)).
thesis.insider_ownership: GMV AG, whose only board members/voting shareholders are Thomas Gard and Stefan Mailänder, previously held 27% of ORBIS AG (2018) before selling down to about 15.36% (2021) as part of the Hörmann transaction ([ORBIS 2021 board report](https://gsc-research.de/media/2021-04-26_ORBIS.pdf)).
thesis.red_flags: Hörmann's stake-building triggered a mandatory takeover offer process (expected around EUR 7.50/share per 2021 analyst commentary); no confirmed squeeze-out or delisting was found in current search results, but concentrated control by a single strategic investor (now near/above 50% with instruments) warrants monitoring for minority-shareholder dilution or a future squeeze-out. [GSC Research ORBIS analysis 2021](https://gsc-research.de/media/2021-04-26_ORBIS.pdf)

thesis.business_description: Papoutsanis S.A., founded in 1870 and based near Athens (Kifissia/Halkida production), manufactures and sells soaps and liquid cosmetics (bar soaps, shower gels, shampoos, hotel amenities, specialty soap bases such as noodles and syndets) under brands including Olivia, Aromatics, Natura and Karavaki Hotel Amenities.
thesis.competitive_position: Papoutsanis describes itself as a leading Greek soap manufacturer and one of the largest producers of bar soap and hotel amenities products in Europe, exporting to Europe, the US, Asia and Oceania. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/PAP.AT/profile/)
thesis.main_shareholders: Reported major shareholders (5%+ voting rights) include Menelaos Tasopoulos (~23.4-23.75%), Georgios Gatzaros (~22.4-23.1%), Truad Verwaltungs AG/Truad Administration Ltd (~21.3%), and 3K Investment Partners (~6.2%). [Athens Times](https://athens-times.com/papoutsanis-at-23-23-the-percentage-of-menelaos-tasopoulos/)
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.

thesis.insider_ownership: High insider/control-vehicle ownership: HPC Vermögensverwaltung GmbH, run by insiders Martin Heuser and Volker Pape, controls approximately 54% of voting rights, with Heuser holding a further ~3.4% personally. [Northdata](https://www.northdata.com/HPC%20Verm%C3%B6gensverwaltung%20GmbH,%20Hannover/HRB%2059094)
thesis.red_flags: FY2025 results showed a negative EBIT of approximately EUR -1.8 million against EUR 81.7 million revenue, attributed to high material inventories and adverse currency effects - a profitability concern worth monitoring, though not a governance or fraud red flag. No governance disputes or auditor concerns were found.

thesis.business_description: Les Docks des Pétroles d'Ambès -SA is a France-based company (Bassens, near Bordeaux) specializing in the storage and transport/loading of petroleum products, including automotive fuels, diesel, and domestic/heavy fuel oil, with storage capacity of up to 270,000 m³, described as one of Europe's largest tank-truck loading facilities. thesis.main_shareholders: Entrepôts Pétroliers Régionaux holds approximately 53.6% (52,445 shares); TotalEnergies SE holds about 12.4% (12,113 shares); Macquarie Strategic Storage Facilities Holdings SARL holds roughly 12.0% (11,701 shares); and Esso S.A.F. holds about 10.0% (9,780 shares). [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/fr/energy/epa-dpam/les-docks-des-petroles-dambes-sa-shares/ownership)
thesis.insider_ownership: Ownership is dominated by large industrial/infrastructure shareholders (Entrepôts Pétroliers Régionaux, TotalEnergies, Macquarie Strategic Storage Facilities, Esso) rather than individual company insiders or a founder-family; President Ahmed Abzizi leads day-to-day management. [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/fr/energy/epa-dpam/les-docks-des-petroles-dambes-sa-shares/ownership)
thesis.red_flags: DPA (then a Total subsidiary) was convicted and ordered to pay approximately €130,000 in damages to the municipality of Macau and three environmental associations following a January 2007 incident in which a crude oil storage tank collapsed and roughly 3,000 m³ of crude oil escaped into the Gironde estuary; this is a documented historical environmental/legal liability tied to the company. [Usine Nouvelle: Docks des pétroles d'Ambès condamnée pour pollution](https://www.usinenouvelle.com/article/docks-des-petroles-d-ambes-filiale-de-total-condamnee-pour-pollution.N890104)

thesis.business_description: Card Factory plc is a UK-based specialist retailer of greeting cards, gifts and celebration essentials, operating through store, online (including Getting Personal), partnership and in-house print (Printcraft) channels.
thesis.competitive_position: Card Factory holds a dominant roughly 33% volume share of the GBP 1.3 billion UK greeting card market (around 20% by value given its low-price positioning), nearly triple its nearest specialist rival, underpinned by producing about 80% of its cards in UK facilities allowing price leadership from 29p while preserving margins. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/card-factory-shares-drop-on-profit-warning-issue-amid-weak-uk-footfall-ce7d50dbd08bf52d)
thesis.main_shareholders: Major institutional holders include Invesco (~27%), Artemis Investment Management (~12%, also cited at ~6.1% in another breakdown), Old Mutual Global Investors (~10%), Aberforth Partners (~10.02%), and BBFIT Investments Pte Ltd (~8.145%). [MarketScreener](https://uk.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/CARD-FACTORY-PLC-16490238/company-shareholders/)
thesis.insider_ownership: No evidence of significant founder/management insider ownership was found; the register is dominated by institutional fund managers rather than board/founder stakes. Not disclosed as a meaningful insider stake in sources reviewed.
thesis.red_flags: The company issued a profit warning in December 2025, cutting adjusted pretax profit guidance for FY2026 to GBP 55-60 million (down from prior guidance of mid-to-high single-digit growth off GBP 66.0 million FY2025), citing weak UK high-street footfall; shares fell around 22% on the announcement. [AJ Bell](https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/card-factory-shares-drop-profit-warning-issue-amid-weak-uk-footfall)

name: SP Group A/S
gmSourceUrl: [SP Group investor relations key figures](https://www.sp-group.com/investor/financial-information/key-figures), [Nasdaq Copenhagen annual report announcement](https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=bf051d29d42359297fedad33d7908f02f&lang=en), [Perplexity Finance SPG.CO](https://perplexity.ai/finance/SPG.CO)

thesis.business_description: SP Group A/S is a Denmark-based plastics processing group manufacturing molded plastic components and coatings for plastic and metal parts, operating factories in Denmark, China, the USA, Latvia, Slovakia, Sweden, Finland, Thailand, and Poland. [SP Group about page](https://www.sp-group.com/about)
thesis.competitive_position: SP Group is described as a leading international supplier of manufactured plastics parts, with global manufacturing scale across nine countries and growing sales; it serves diverse industrial end markets rather than a single customer segment, which diversifies its competitive exposure. [TPI-Polytechniek: About SP Group](https://www.tpi-polytechniek.com/about-sp-group/)
thesis.main_shareholders: Major shareholders include Chairman Hans Wilhelm Schur (~17.35%), CEO Frank Marius Gad (~10.01%), ODIN Forvaltning AS (~8.67%), and Arbejdsmarkedets Tillægspension/ATP (~7.38%). [MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/SP-GROUP-A-S-43257883/company/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is notably high for a listed industrial company: Chairman Hans Wilhelm Schur holds about 17.35% and CEO Frank Gad holds about 10.01%, together representing over a quarter of the company held by its top two governance figures. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/SP-GROUP-A-S-43257883/company/)
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources searched; SP Group discloses compliance with Danish corporate governance recommendations on a comply-or-explain basis. [SP Group corporate governance](https://www.sp-group.com/investor/corporate-governance)

thesis.business_description: Transilvania Broker de Asigurare S.A. is a Romanian insurance brokerage, intermediating insurance policies (life, health, property/casualty) between insurers and retail/corporate clients, listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange (BVB) since November 2017.
thesis.competitive_position: TBK is one of the larger independent insurance brokers listed on the Romanian market; it recently attracted a strategic Czech financial-services acquirer (Partners Financial Services), signaling perceived value in its distribution network within the Romanian insurance intermediation market. [Forbes Romania on PFS majority stake](https://www.forbes.ro/?p=521261)
thesis.main_shareholders: Partners Financial Services a.s. (Czech Republic) is now the majority shareholder, having raised its stake from 39.09% to 53.24% of share capital and voting rights (per a September 2026 BVB filing) ([BVB current report](https://m.bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/TBK_20260827164403_TBK-Raport-Semestrul-I-2026.pdf)); it initially acquired ~32.89% in July 2024 by buying shares from founders Gabriel Login and Dan Niculae ([Ziarul Financiar](https://www.zf.ro/burse-fonduri-mutuale/bursa-mesajul-cehilor-care-au-devenit-actionari-majoritari-ai-22428555)).
thesis.insider_ownership: Co-founders Gabriel Login and Dan Niculae remain minority holders after selling down: Login's stake fell from 36.14% to about 14.14% and Niculae's from 15.69% to about 9.79% following the July 2024 sale to Partners Financial Services ([Ziarul Financiar](https://www.zf.ro/burse-fonduri-mutuale/bursa-login-gabriel-si-niculae-dan-actionarii-semnificativi-ai-22425950)).
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; no litigation or governance dispute was found connecting Transilvania Broker or Partners Financial Services (note: unrelated company SIF Transilvania has an extensive, well-documented litigation history, but this does not pertain to Transilvania Broker de Asigurare - the two are separate entities despite similar names).

thesis.business_description: German family-run bank (founded 1983 by Uto Baader) providing market making, capital markets/IPO advisory, multi-asset brokerage, asset management services, banking services and research, headquartered in Unterschleißheim.
thesis.competitive_position: A local broker/market maker in the DACH region acting as lead broker for quoting and executing orders across 800,000+ financial instruments; total assets of €3.235bn and 677 employees (2025), positioning it as a niche capital-markets infrastructure player rather than a universal bank.
thesis.main_shareholders: Baader family (via Baader Beteiligungs AG) controls 71.7% of shares; remainder held by private/institutional investors and management/employees ([Grokipedia/company disclosures](https://www.baaderbank.de/en/about-us/investor-relations/equity-story))
thesis.insider_ownership: Baader family controls approximately 71.7% of shares; founder Uto Baader handed management to son Nico Baader in July 2015 ([Baader Bank](https://www.baaderbank.de/en/about-us/investor-relations/equity-story))
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources; concentrated family control (71.7%) limits free float and outside shareholder influence.

thesis.business_description: Oeneo SA is a French company and self-described world No.1 in cooperage for winemaking and world No.2 in wine-bottle closures, operating via two segments: Closures (including its DIAM technology) and Barrels (ageing solutions for wine and spirits). [Cork Maker Regains Sparkle - Wine-Searcher](https://www.wine-searcher.com/m/2012/10/cork-maker-oeneo-diam-closures-success)
thesis.competitive_position: Oeneo holds global leadership positions in both wine barrel cooperage (No.1) and wine closures (No.2, via its patented DIAM cork-alternative technology), giving it a scale/technology moat in a specialized wine- and spirits-industry supply niche. [Wine-Searcher: Cork Maker Regains Sparkle](https://www.wine-searcher.com/m/2012/10/cork-maker-oeneo-diam-closures-success)
thesis.main_shareholders: Andromède SAS (controlled by the Hériard Dubreuil family) holds a controlling stake, historically built up to approximately 63.1%-71.6% of Oeneo's capital and voting rights through its subsidiary Caspar; other shareholders include Tetragon Partners UK LLP (~17.59%) and Lazard Frères Gestion SAS (~2.06%). [MarketScreener shareholders](https://in.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/OENEO-151073694/company-shareholders/)
thesis.insider_ownership: The Hériard Dubreuil family, via Andromède SAS/Caspar, is the controlling insider shareholder, holding a majority stake (reported between ~63% and ~72% depending on the date) and having previously launched a tender offer with squeeze-out procedure for remaining shares, overseen by an independent expert (Eight Advisory). [Caspar tender offer filing](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Caspar-has-filed-a-draft-simplified-tender-offer-for-Oeneo-shares-with-the-AMF-29707871/)
thesis.red_flags: Oeneo was subject to a simplified tender offer plus potential squeeze-out by its controlling shareholder (Caspar/Andromède, Hériard Dubreuil family); an independent expert and ad hoc board committee were used to assess fairness, which is a standard minority-protection process but worth noting as a controlling-shareholder related transaction. [Tender offer and squeeze-out details](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Caspar-has-filed-a-draft-simplified-tender-offer-for-Oeneo-shares-with-the-AMF-29707871/)

thesis.business_description: French software company (headquartered in Boulogne-Billancourt) providing an AI-native Order-to-Cash (O2C) SaaS platform - including AI agent 'Aimie' - that predicts customer payment behavior, automates cash-collection and dematerializes B2B transactions.
thesis.competitive_position: Positioned by Gartner as a Leader in the Magic Quadrant for Invoice-to-Cash applications; global leader in AI-powered Order-to-Cash software with clients in 85+ countries; 2025 revenue of €61.4M with North America now 30% of subscription revenue, and management targeting €18-23M in AI-native revenue with 185-215% CAGR through 2030.
thesis.main_shareholders: Olivier Novasque (founder/CEO, 37.8%, 533,844 shares), Herald Investment Management Ltd (3.98%), Deka Investment GmbH (2.83%); top 16 shareholders own 48.76% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/fr/software/epa-albfr/sidetrade-shares/ownership))
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder and CEO Olivier Novasque holds approximately 37.8% of shares, giving him effective control ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/fr/software/epa-albfr/sidetrade-shares/ownership))
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Aspo Oyj is a Finland-based conglomerate (holding company) that owns and develops several business-to-business brands, including ESL Shipping (dry bulk shipping), Leipurin (bakery ingredients), Telko (plastics/chemicals distribution), and Kaukomarkkinat. [Aspo Oyj company overview](https://www.aspo.com/)
thesis.competitive_position: Aspo is a diversified Nordic industrial/trading conglomerate whose segments each hold established regional positions (e.g., ESL Shipping in Baltic/Nordic dry bulk shipping); the company recently approved a demerger plan to separate ESL Shipping (in which Aspo holds a 78.6% stake) into its own independently listed company, a structural unbundling intended to let the market value each business more clearly. [Aspo stock exchange release: ESL Shipping demerger plan](https://www.aspo.com/stock-exchange-releases/inside-information-the-board-of-directors-of-aspo-plc-has-approved-a-demerger-plan-concerning-the-separation-of-esl-shipping-into-a-new-listed-company-3337215)
thesis.main_shareholders: Major shareholders include the Nyberg Family (~10.86%), AEV Capital Holding Oy (~10.49%), pension insurer Keskinäinen Työeläkevakuutusyhtiö Varma (~4.53%), Tapio Vehmas (~4.06%), and pension insurer Keskinäinen Eläkevakuutusyhtiö Ilmarinen (~2.79%). [MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ASPO-OYJ-1412432/company/)
thesis.insider_ownership: The Nyberg family is the largest named insider/founder-linked holder at approximately 10.86%; individual holder Tapio Vehmas (~4.06%) is also a notable named shareholder, though overall insider concentration is moderate compared to many other companies in this batch. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ASPO-OYJ-1412432/company/)
thesis.red_flags: Aspo disclosed that its ESL Shipping and Leipurin units suspended/reduced operations in Russia following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine (a disclosed compliance action, not a governance scandal); no lawsuit or fraud allegation was identified in the sources searched. [Leave Russia tracker: Aspo](https://leave-russia.org/aspo)

thesis.business_description: Lion Capital S.A. (formerly SIF Banat-Crișana) is a Romanian closed-end financial investment company (a former 'SIF') that holds a diversified portfolio of equity stakes, including a near-100% stake in real-estate vehicle SIF Imobiliare.
thesis.competitive_position: One of Romania's legacy privatization-era investment funds (SIFs), trading at a persistent discount to net asset value typical of the SIF sector; governance has been contested by minority shareholder groups. [Lion Capital Key Information](https://www.lion-capital.ro/en/about-lion-capital/key-information/)
thesis.main_shareholders: Infinity Capital Investments SA holds approximately 20%; broader shareholder base split roughly between Romanian legal entities (~45.10%), Romanian individuals (~39.73%), non-resident legal entities (~13.80%) and non-resident individuals (~1.36%) as of September 2025, across roughly 5.7 million shareholders typical of ex-SIF mass-privatization registers. [Lion Capital BoD Report 2025](https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/LION_20260327175146_BoD-Report-2025.pdf)
thesis.insider_ownership: Chairman and CEO Bogdan-Alexandru Drăgoi leads management; minority shareholder group Blue Capital (~8.63%) and the Association of SIF Investors (AISIF) have publicly alleged management operates in its own interest rather than reflecting a transparent insider ownership stake. Not clearly disclosed as a specific management ownership percentage. [Bursa.ro](https://www.bursa.ro/aisif-blue-capital-cel-mai-mare-actionar-real-al-lion-capital-a-ajuns-neputincios-in-mainile-unui-management-care-urmareste-exclusiv-interesele-proprii-82983259)
thesis.red_flags: Significant governance disputes: minority shareholder Blue Capital and AISIF (Association of SIF Investors) have publicly accused management of acting in self-interest and of inventing reasons to withhold dividends; Lion Capital's president won a court case annulling an ASF fine over alleged coordinated action with SIF Muntenia; the company was also sued (and the suit later withdrawn) by London-based Lion Capital LLP over use of the 'Lion Capital' name. [Bursa.ro](https://www.bursa.ro/aisif-blue-capital-cel-mai-mare-actionar-real-al-lion-capital-a-ajuns-neputincios-in-mainile-unui-management-care-urmareste-exclusiv-interesele-proprii-82983259)

thesis.business_description: Spanish designer, manufacturer and marketer (founded 2002, headquartered in Álava) of ball and roller bearings and industrial components for cranes, offshore machinery, wind power, railway, gearboxes and heavy industrial equipment.
thesis.competitive_position: A specialized industrial bearings manufacturer with ~345 employees serving diverse heavy-industry end markets (wind, rail, oil & gas, mining, steel); maintains a strategic partnership/equity relationship with Chinese bearings manufacturer Cronos, giving it manufacturing scale support versus larger global bearing makers (SKF, Schaeffler, Timken).
thesis.main_shareholders: Controlled by Pakel RMI Promoción de Empresas SL; co-founders are also majority shareholders and hold an equity stake in the related Chinese partner Cronos; listed on Spain's MAB/BME Growth market since 2015 with stable core shareholders ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/NBI-BEARINGS-EUROPE-S-A-105514996/company-shareholders/))
thesis.insider_ownership: Co-founders hold majority equity as core/controlling shareholders (via Pakel RMI Promoción de Empresas SL); specific % not disclosed in available sources ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/NBI-BEARINGS-EUROPE-S-A-105514996/company-shareholders/))
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: Socfinaf S.A., based in Luxembourg and founded in 1890, produces, processes and sells palm oil and natural rubber through agro-industrial plantations in Sierra Leone, Liberia, Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana, Nigeria, Cameroon, São Tomé and Príncipe and the Republic of Congo.
thesis.competitive_position: Socfinaf is part of the broader Socfin group, one of the largest palm-oil/rubber plantation operators in Africa, managing a substantial share of the group's more than 190,600 hectares of tropical plantations; 2025 revenue grew 8.5% to EUR641.9m, though earnings fell 17% to EUR47.1m ([StockAnalysis](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/lux/SOFAF/)).
thesis.main_shareholders: SOCFIN (58.85%) and Bolloré (9%) as of 2018 disclosures; SOCFIN itself is controlled by the Fabri family (approximately 52-55%) and Bolloré Participations (approximately 38-40%) ([Tresor.economie.gouv.fr / GRAIN corporate structure report](https://www.grain.org/system/attachments/sources/000/005/823/original/The_corporate_structure_Socfin_EN.pdf))
thesis.insider_ownership: Not separately disclosed for Socfinaf itself; ultimate control runs through SOCFIN, which is majority-owned by the Fabri family and the Bolloré group ([GRAIN corporate structure report](https://www.grain.org/system/attachments/sources/000/005/823/original/The_corporate_structure_Socfin_EN.pdf))
thesis.red_flags: Socfin group plantations (including Socfinaf subsidiaries in West/Central Africa) have faced sustained allegations from NGOs and local communities of land-rights violations, lack of free-prior-informed-consent, water pollution, and gender-based violence by plantation security, per investigations by Earthsight, Mongabay and the Business & Human Rights Resource Centre ([Earthsight](https://www.earthsight.org.uk/news/idm/socfin-under-scrutiny-alleged-abuses-africa-rubber-palm-oil-plantations-despite-pldeges); [Mongabay](https://news.mongabay.com/2025/03/new-allegations-of-abuse-against-oil-palm-giant-socfin-in-cameroon/)).

thesis.business_description: Aplisens S.A. is a Polish manufacturer of industrial process instrumentation, specializing in pressure and differential-pressure transmitters, hydrostatic level probes, level transmitters, temperature sensors, valves and digital indicators used across power, chemical, refining, pharmaceutical and food industries.
thesis.competitive_position: Aplisens describes itself as a leading domestic (Polish) manufacturer and integrator of industrial measurement and control instrumentation, operating six manufacturing plants in Poland plus a branch in Belarus, and selling across the EU, CIS countries (historically including Russia/Belarus/Ukraine) and Asia — giving it a strong niche position in a fragmented, technically specialized market rather than true global scale. [Aplisens - Group overview](https://aplisens.com/grupa-aplisens.html); [Aplisens - About us](https://aplisens.com/ofirmie.html).
thesis.main_shareholders: According to aggregator data sourced from the company's official shareholder-structure disclosures, the largest holders are CEO Adam Żurawski (~27.53%), Mirosław Dawidonis (~13.16%), Sławomir Szewczyk (~11.56%), Mirosław Karczmarczyk (~10.22%), Andrzej Kobiałka (~9.79%) and Dorota Zubkow (~8.82%); together these six hold roughly 81% of shares. [Aplisens - Struktura Akcjonariatu (official)](https://aplisens.pl/struktura-akcjonariatu.html); [BiznesRadar - Aplisens shareholding](https://www.biznesradar.pl/akcjonariat/APLISENS).
thesis.insider_ownership: Ownership is heavily insider-concentrated: CEO Adam Żurawski alone holds roughly 27.5%, and the named individual shareholders above (all appearing to be founding management/engineers) collectively control over 80% of the company, leaving a small free float. [Aplisens - Struktura Akcjonariatu](https://aplisens.pl/struktura-akcjonariatu.html).
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources. No litigation, auditor disputes, or related-party controversies surfaced in available search results; note the company historically had exposure to Russia/Belarus/CIS markets via its Belarus manufacturing branch, which is a geopolitical/sanctions-risk consideration rather than a governance red flag. [Aplisens - Group overview](https://aplisens.com/grupa-aplisens.html).

thesis.business_description: cBrain A/S is a Danish software company providing the F2 digital platform, a commercial off-the-shelf case- and document-management system used by government ministries, agencies and municipalities for workflow, compliance, FOI/records management and (more recently) AI-assisted case handling.
thesis.competitive_position: cBrain's F2 platform is used by more than 75 Danish government bodies including 21 of Denmark's ministries, giving it a dominant, deeply entrenched position in the Danish central-government case-management market; it has also expanded F2 to over a dozen other countries (including France, Germany, the UK, the US, the UAE and several African nations), positioning it as a scalable COTS alternative to costly bespoke government IT systems. [cBrain company profile - stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/cph/CBRAIN/company/); [Investseekers - cBrain: A Scalable Software Play for the Public Sector](https://www.investseekers.com/post/cbrain-a-scalable-software-play-for-the-public-sector).
thesis.main_shareholders: Founder and CEO Per Tejs Knudsen is the dominant shareholder, holding approximately 41.7% of shares (~8.34 million shares); other holders include CTO Thomas Qvist (~3.58%), ODIN Forvaltning AS (~3%) and Nordea Investment Management AB (~1.9%). The company has approximately 14,200 shareholders across 40 countries. [cBrain - Ownership (official)](https://www.cbrain.com/investor/ownership).
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is very high and founder-concentrated: CEO/founder Per Tejs Knudsen controls approximately 41.7% of the company and CTO Thomas Qvist holds approximately 3.58%, together representing roughly 45% of shares held by two senior executives. [cBrain - Ownership (official)](https://www.cbrain.com/investor/ownership); [theorg.com - Per Tejs Knudsen, CEO/Founder](https://theorg.com/org/cbrain/org-chart/per-tejs-knudsen).
thesis.red_flags: No major controversy identified. Routine insider share sales by CEO Per Tejs Knudsen (e.g., a sale of 192,730 shares, ~0.96% of market cap, reported April 2024) and an earlier combined sale of a 4.2% stake by Knudsen and Qvist to institutional investors were found, but these were disclosed PDMR transactions rather than signs of distress or governance failure. None identified from official sources beyond routine, disclosed insider trading. [cBrain - PDMR transaction report](https://www.cbrain.com/post/reporting-of-executive-employees-trading-in-cbrain-shares).

thesis.business_description: Mo-BRUK S.A. is a Polish company specializing in hazardous and non-hazardous industrial waste management, including solidification/stabilization of inorganic waste, incineration of hazardous and medical waste, and production of alternative fuels.
thesis.competitive_position: A leading Polish hazardous-waste treatment and incineration operator, founded in 1985 by Józef Mokrzycki, occupying a specialist niche in regulated waste disposal infrastructure in Poland. [Mo-BRUK corporate ESDD report](https://mobruk.pl/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/MoBRUKCorporateESDDfinalreport221112.pdf)
thesis.main_shareholders: The Mokrzycki family (via holding vehicle Ginger Capital) holds approximately 20%; other large holders include PTE Allianz Polska (~7.6%), Nationale-Nederlanden OFE (~6.98%), PTE PZU (~6.0%), and PKO BP Bankowy PTE (~5.1%). [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/MO-BRUK-S-A-124007838/company-shareholders/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder Józef Mokrzycki and family remain the largest shareholder group at approximately 20% through Ginger Capital, though he stepped down as Chairman of the Board in June 2022 after 37 years leading the company. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/MO-BRUK-S-A-124007838/company-shareholders/)
thesis.red_flags: The company has been in a multi-year tax dispute with Polish authorities over retroactively increased landfill fees at its Wałbrzych site (2016-2020 periods), which led to a PLN 65.2m provision and a temporary PLN 2.5m bank account freeze in December 2023; some claims (2016, 2020) were later overturned in Mo-BRUK's favor, but disputes for 2018-2019 remain unresolved. [Stockwatch.pl](https://www.stockwatch.pl/wiadomosci/mo-bruk-sko-umarza-ponad-122-mln-zl-podwyzszonych-oplat,akcje,363816)

thesis.business_description: Bijou Brigitte modische Accessoires AG is a Hamburg-based retailer that manufactures, imports and sells fashion jewelry, gold and silver jewelry, and fashion accessories through its own store chains across Germany and other European markets.
thesis.competitive_position: A long-established European fashion-accessories chain retailer (founded 1987) deriving the majority of revenue from Germany, with additional store networks in Spain, Italy and Portugal; revenue of roughly EUR 225 million in 2025 with operating margin under pressure (7.3% vs 10.2% prior year) amid cautious German consumer sentiment. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/bijou-brigitte-modische-accessoires-annual-report-2025-incl-consolidated-financial-statements-co-ce7f5adadc8cfe21)
thesis.main_shareholders: Founder-related holder Friedrich-Wilhelm Werner is reported to own approximately 53% of the company; the general public/free float holds roughly 43%, with Dimensional Fund Advisors and Ennismore Fund Management among other notable holders. [Yahoo Finance/Simply Wall St](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/bijou-brigitte-modische-accessoires-aktiengesellschaft-070951105.html)
thesis.insider_ownership: Insider ownership is high and concentrated, with Friedrich-Wilhelm Werner reported to hold approximately 53% of shares, giving insiders a controlling stake. [Yahoo Finance/Simply Wall St](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/bijou-brigitte-modische-accessoires-aktiengesellschaft-070951105.html)
thesis.red_flags: An internal investigation confirmed a service provider committed invoice fraud against the company, prompting a forensic examination; separately, Supervisory Board chairmanship changed in June 2025 (Marianne Tochtermann replacing Friedhelm Steinberg) amid declining margins. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/bijou-brigitte-modische-accessoires-annual-report-2025-incl-consolidated-financial-statements-co-ce7f5adadc8cfe21)

thesis.business_description: Scandi Standard AB is a Sweden-based poultry company and the largest producer of chicken-based food products in the Nordic region, operating via Kronfågel (Sweden), Scandinavian Standard/Cardinal Foods (Norway), and Danpo (Denmark), with additional operations in Ireland and the Netherlands. [Matrix BCG company history](https://matrixbcg.com/blogs/brief-history/scandistandard)
thesis.competitive_position: Scandi Standard holds a leading position as the largest Nordic chicken producer, built through consolidation of national poultry champions (Kronfågel, Danpo, Cardinal Foods); it has continued to expand via acquisitions (Irish, Danish, Dutch poultry assets), though it has faced margin pressure from rising feed/raw material costs and Netherlands start-up costs. [Scandi Standard: A Chicken Empire in Transition](https://parsers.vc/news/241022-scandi-standard--a-chicken-empire-in/)
thesis.main_shareholders: Major shareholders include Lusiaves SGPS SA (~21.29%), Investment AB Öresund (~15.29%), Lantmännen Animalieinvest AB (~10.57%), and Nordea Investment Management AB (~6.23%). [MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/SCANDI-STANDARD-AB-16817052/company-shareholders/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Not disclosed as a specific management/board insider percentage separate from the large institutional/strategic holders (Lusiaves, Öresund, Lantmännen) listed above; no distinct founder/management stake was found. Could not verify further.
thesis.red_flags: No profit-warning scandal or governance controversy was identified; the company has faced normal operating headwinds (rising chicken feed costs, Netherlands start-up costs) but these are disclosed business factors, not governance red flags. [Scandi Standard interim report Jan-Dec 2025](https://investors.scandistandard.com/en/reports/scandi-standards-ab-publ-interim-report-january-december-2025)

thesis.business_description: High Co. SA (HighCo) is a France-based marketing services group providing data marketing and communication solutions for mass-market retailers and consumer goods manufacturers, including coupon issuance, sampling, point-of-sale marketing, and digital marketing services. [Turning Rough Stones: High Co SA overview](https://turningroughstones.substack.com/p/high-co-sa-cheap-french-marketing)
thesis.competitive_position: HighCo operates primarily in France (over 80% of revenue) with additional operations in Spain, the UK, Poland, Russia, and Turkey, serving retailers and CPG brands in promotional/data marketing; it is backed by a large strategic shareholder (WPP), giving it scale/network advantages versus independent promotional agencies, though it remains a smaller-cap player relative to global marketing holding companies. [HighCo company profile - MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/HIGHCO-5002/company/)
thesis.main_shareholders: WPP France Holdings (part of the UK-listed WPP Group) holds approximately 37.4%; Eximium, controlled by the Baulé family, holds about 11.3%; Gérard de Bartillat Participations holds roughly 5.1%; management and employees hold about 3.2% combined. [Turning Rough Stones: High Co SA overview](https://turningroughstones.substack.com/p/high-co-sa-cheap-french-marketing)
thesis.insider_ownership: The chairman personally owns approximately 1.85% of shares, and management/employees collectively hold about 3.2%; the Baulé family's Eximium vehicle (~11.3%) represents a further insider/founder-linked holding distinct from the large external strategic shareholder WPP. [Turning Rough Stones](https://turningroughstones.substack.com/p/high-co-sa-cheap-french-marketing)
thesis.red_flags: No lawsuit or governance controversy specific to HighCo SA was identified in the sources searched; note that parent/large shareholder WPP Group has faced separate, unrelated corporate controversies (a 2021 SEC FCPA settlement, and 2025-era shareholder/whistleblower lawsuits at the group level), but no evidence was found connecting these to HighCo SA itself. [WPP SEC settlement](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2021-191)

thesis.business_description: Bio Planet S.A., founded in 2005 and based in Leszno/Wilkowa Wieś, Poland, produces, packages and distributes organic/ecological food for humans and animals (around 4,000 products) under its own Bio Planet brand and third-party brands such as Alce Nero and Bio Planète, both in Poland and internationally.
thesis.competitive_position: Bio Planet is a specialist Polish organic-food producer and distributor with a broad product catalogue (~4,000 SKUs), positioning it as a scaled player in Poland's organic/health-food niche rather than a mainstream grocery supplier. [EMIS company profile](https://www.emis.com/php/company-profile/PL/Bio_Planet_SA_en_3379542.html)
thesis.main_shareholders: Ownership is concentrated among founders under a shareholders' agreement: Grzegorz Mulik (~19.36%), Barbara Mariola Strużyna (~18.53%), Mariusz Krzysztof Ziemiańczyk (~10.5%), GK4 Food sp. z o.o. (~10%), Bio Pole sp. z o.o. (~8%) and Sylwester Strużyna (~7.17%). [BiznesRadar](https://www.biznesradar.pl/akcjonariat/BIO-PLANET)
thesis.insider_ownership: Founders and supervisory board members (Grzegorz, Maciej and Michał Mulik, and the Strużyna family) collectively control a majority of shares under a formal shareholders' agreement, representing high founder/insider concentration (combined founder-linked stakes exceed 50%). [BiznesRadar](https://www.biznesradar.pl/akcjonariat/BIO-PLANET)
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources.

thesis.business_description: A.P.N. Promise S.A. is a Polish IT services company (incorporated 1991, headquartered in Warsaw) providing software licensing, implementation and consulting services to large and medium enterprises, public administration and healthcare clients.
thesis.competitive_position: A Polish IT licensing/consulting reseller and systems integrator serving enterprise and public-sector clients, including partnership/distribution deals such as with Allegro; specific market-share data was not found in sources reviewed. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/A-P-N-PROMISE-S-A-47418961/company/)
thesis.main_shareholders: CEO Piotr Paszczyk directly owns approximately 57.24% of shares (worth roughly PLN 52.17m); other major holders include Tomasz Bator (~13.7% personally plus a further ~8.6% via a related entity), and Paweł Kołakowski (~10.2%). [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/pl/software/wse-pro/apn-promise-shares/ownership)
thesis.insider_ownership: Very high insider/founder ownership: CEO Piotr Paszczyk (appointed January 1998) holds approximately 57.24% of shares, giving him effective control of the company. [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/pl/software/wse-pro/apn-promise-shares/ownership)
thesis.red_flags: None identified from official sources in available search results.

name: Manx Financial Group PLC
gmSourceUrl: [Manx Financial Group 2024 Annual Report](https://mfg.im/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/manx-financial-group-plc-ar-web-1.pdf), [Manx Financial Group 2023 Annual Report](https://mfg.im/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/manx-financial-group-annual-report-2023-2.pdf)

thesis.business_description: Manx Financial Group PLC is an Isle of Man-based financial services holding company whose main subsidiary, Conister Bank, provides retail and commercial banking, lending and related financial services to customers in the Isle of Man and the UK.
thesis.competitive_position: Manx Financial Group is a small specialist/niche lender operating through Conister Bank, competing in UK and Isle of Man commercial and consumer finance (including asset finance and newly regulated BNPL) against larger UK specialist lenders; its small market capitalization (~£28m) limits scale and share liquidity relative to peers.
thesis.main_shareholders: Jim Mellon and Burnbrae Group Limited (beneficial owner) ~18.18%, Gregory Bailey (second-largest individual shareholder) ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/MANX-FINANCIAL-GROUP-PLC-4007820/company/))
thesis.insider_ownership: Chairman Jim Mellon and affiliated Burnbrae Group hold ~18.18%; additional board members (Gregory Bailey, Douglas Grant and others) hold further undisclosed amounts, so a full insider aggregate was not found
thesis.red_flags: FY2025 profit before tax fell 26% after a £1.3m provision tied to the FCA's motor finance discretionary-commission review (cumulative provision £1.5m), with the final FCA redress scheme still uncertain; credit impairments nearly doubled in 2025 against a relatively thin £43.6m equity base, and management described conditions as "fragile." ([Kalkine](https://kalkine.co.uk/news/general-news/why-manx-financial-group-plc-mfx-could-be-a-uk-financial-stock-to-watch-in-2026))

thesis.business_description: Prime Office A/S is a Denmark-headquartered real estate company focused on acquiring, developing, and managing commercial office and residential properties, primarily in large German cities (population above 200,000), through its subsidiary PO Holding Germany GmbH and various German property subsidiaries. [MarketScreener company profile](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/PRIME-OFFICE-A-S-3782467/company/)
thesis.competitive_position: Prime Office is a small-cap, Denmark-listed vehicle for German commercial/residential property investment founded in 2007 by Mogens Møller; it operates in the challenged German office real estate market, which independent analysts (e.g., Moody's) have flagged as facing a widening quality gap and broader softness. [Bloomberg: German Property Slump to Widen Office Quality Gap](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-02-28/german-property-slump-to-widen-office-quality-gap-moody-s-says)
thesis.main_shareholders: Major shareholders include founder Mogens Vinther Møller (~27.25%), AHJ A/S (~15.72%), BD Invest ApS (~11.01%), and Kjell Bugge (~10.01%). [MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/PRIME-OFFICE-A-S-39433697/company-shareholders/)
thesis.insider_ownership: Founder Mogens Vinther Møller remains the largest named shareholder at approximately 27.25%, indicating high founder/insider concentration. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/PRIME-OFFICE-A-S-39433697/company-shareholders/)
